With Kevin Warsh now confirmed as Federal Reserve Chairman, the real work to fix affordability begins — and Congress must step up. 💪

Warsh was one of the few at the Fed who strongly opposed Quantitative Easing (QE) from the beginning. For those unfamiliar, QE is when the Federal Reserve creates trillions of dollars out of thin air to buy bonds and other assets, flooding the economy with cheap money. 💰

He warned it would create a “reverse Robin Hood” effect: inflating massive asset bubbles that make the wealthy richer while impoverishing everyone without assets.  This a major root cause of why housing costs are so expensive 📈➡️🏦

I was working at the center of the financial crisis as a restructuring professional, and I knew he was right the moment QE became the norm. History proved it. This is one of the two root causes of the affordability crisis crushing middle-class families today. The other is the armies of middlemen driving up costs in healthcare. 🏥

The Fed’s current dual mandate of maximum employment and stable prices is outdated and incomplete. As a Congressman, I will push legislation that inserts Congress into this conversation and expands the Fed’s mandate to explicitly include a third goal: helping the majority of Americans — the middle class — own their homes outright. 🏠

Homeownership is the foundation of generational wealth, and Fed policy has made it nearly impossible for too many families.
Warsh is already focused on shrinking the Fed’s bloated balance sheet. There’s no easy path, but we can repair the damage from QE by creating a targeted program of zero-interest home loans for first-time buyers and families who currently have little or no assets. These loans would amortize over 15 years and eventually help shrink the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet. 🔄

This isn’t just about fixing affordability — it’s about giving millions of hardworking Americans a real opportunity to own their home and build lasting wealth for their families, just like previous generations did. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦

If elected to Congress, I will fight to:
• Expand the Fed’s mandate to prioritize middle-class homeownership 🏡
• Support zero-interest home loans to undo the harm of QE
• Hold the Fed accountable to the people it serves, not just Wall Street

The era of trickle-down monetary policy is over. It’s time for policies that actually lift up the middle class. 🇺🇸

What do you think? Should Congress expand the Fed’s mandate to make widespread homeownership a national priority?
